🟡 **Export button shows a checkmark emoji, breaking the project's no-emoji rule** A checkmark emoji character is placed into the export button's success text (`'✓ Exportado'` at `export/glbExporter.js:105`), which is generated output shown to the user, violating the project's explicit "No emojis in source, docs, or generated output" rule. Impact: The shipped UI displays an emoji that the repository's contribution rules forbid.
Rule source and location `CONTRIBUTING.md` states under Development: "No emojis in source, docs, or generated output." The success state text at `export/glbExporter.js:105` uses `✓` (U+2713). This is both in source and rendered as generated UI output.
```suggestion button.textContent = 'Exportado'; ``` --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

🟡 **Export button shows a warning emoji, breaking the project's no-emoji rule** A warning-sign emoji character is placed into the export button's error text (`'⚠ Error'` at `export/glbExporter.js:109`), which is generated output shown to the user, violating the project's explicit "No emojis in source, docs, or generated output" rule. Impact: The shipped UI displays an emoji that the repository's contribution rules forbid.
Rule source and location `CONTRIBUTING.md` states under Development: "No emojis in source, docs, or generated output." The error state text at `export/glbExporter.js:109` uses `⚠` (U+26A0), an emoji, in both source and rendered UI output.
```suggestion button.textContent = 'Error'; ``` --- *Was this helpful? React with 👍 or 👎 to provide feedback.*

`Path.read_text()` uses the platform default encoding; since this is JSON (UTF-8 by spec), it’s safer and more portable (e.g., on Windows) to read with an explicit UTF-8 encoding. Consider making the same encoding explicit for the corresponding `write_text()` call later in this block as well.
Fixed in c2c77e5: spec JSON now uses explicit UTF-8 for both read and write, with regression coverage.

`cv2` / `numpy` against `CONTRIBUTING.md:28` — *"Scripts are pure Python 3.10+ standard library. No pip dependencies."* Same at `:139`, `feature_matcher.py:119`, `pose_estimator.py:105`.

The lazy import inside the function means it degrades instead of crashing, which is the right behaviour — but the stdlib fallback is then the only path that ever runs here, so ~986 lines of SfM core reach nothing but their fallback.

Either declare the optional dep explicitly in `docs/multi-view-synthesis.md` and gate the metric path on it, or drop the SfM core and keep view counting + dedup, which are the parts that earned their place on a real run.

This is the concrete cost of the dep gate. On an 8-view run the brief came back `poseConfidence: 0.0211`, `depthConfidence: 0.0`, `calibratedDepthAvailable: false`, `components: {}`.

The module reported that honestly, which I want to credit — but worth deciding whether the metric path ships as opt-in or does not ship.

Vocabulary gap, found on real filenames.

- no `iso` / `oblique` / `three-quarter` class at all, so a three-quarter view has nowhere to go
- bare `side` is not an alias — only `side-left` / `side-right` — so `view-side-elevation.png` matched nothing and fell through to its raw filename

My set was four three-quarters + three orthographic elevations, and the classifier could not represent either category.

First-match-wins over `VIEW_NAMES` dict order is the bug.

The token regex below is correct — the `frontier` / `leftover` fix works. But `view-iso-front-right-a` contains both `front` and `right` as delimited tokens; `front` is first in the dict, so every three-quarter view classified as a front elevation.

Result on 8 real views: `namedViews` = `front`, `front-2` ... `front-6`, `back`, `view-side-elevation` — six of eight labelled front, including all four isos **and** both orthographic elevations.

Suggest collecting every matching token and resolving by specificity rather than returning on the first dict hit.

`duplicateViewCount` is not a duplicate count — it is `input - len(grouped_views)`, and `group_duplicate_views` groups by **name**. So the naming collapse at `view_counter.py:136` propagates straight into this field.

Measured: this reported `duplicateViewCount: 5` on a set where `check_reference_admission.py` rejected exactly **1** true near-duplicate (`view-iso-front-right-c`, pHash within 6). Four of the five were distinct views collapsed by the same-name bug.

Fixing `view_counter.py:136` fixes this too — same root cause, two symptoms. Might still be worth renaming the field to say what it measures.

stage1b -> stage4 back-edge: an intake-stage module importing a review-stage module at module level. `feature_detector.py:188` does the same with `make_comparison_sheet`.

Also a third import convention in the tree — the rest of `forge/` uses `sys.path.insert(...)` + flat module imports with `# noqa: E402` (`diagnose_render.py:29-36`), while this package uses relative imports plus one absolute `forge.` path. Worth settling on one before the layering sets.

`components` is `{}` in `evidence-only` mode, and `{} in brief` is True — so this branch is entered on every real run and enhances nothing.

Not a crash, but it means `brief_enhancer` / `build_enhancer` / `review_enhancer` / `hybrid_synthesis` (~830 lines) have no input in the only mode the module currently reaches. Worth a guard on non-empty, and a note in the docs that these activate only once calibrated geometry exists.

This checklist cannot be satisfied in the mode the module actually ships in. "Poses estimated with reasonable accuracy" and "Depth data generated" both require the metric path; on my run they were 0.0211 and 0.0, `status: evidence-only`, and the reconstruction still succeeded.

Suggest splitting into an evidence-only checklist and a calibrated checklist, so the gate matches the module's real default.

"Misaligned Views" is about geometric misalignment solved by RANSAC. The harder case is views that **disagree about the object**, and nothing in this doc or `grimoire/multi_view/` covers it.

My set's three orthographic elevations disagreed by ~8% on overall width and implied two different depths, so no single consistent 3D form could satisfy all of them. Resolving that by hand was ~40 min — the largest single block in a 3.5 h run, and the one place multiple views created work instead of saving it.

A "Contradictory views" section would be the highest-value addition here: pick one view as the metric authority, calibrate against a real-world prior, record every conflict as an explicit assumption, and state plainly when the set cannot be satisfied.

This table describes what each view count unlocks, but not what the *environment* has to provide. Worth stating here that `full`/`optimal` metric output additionally requires `cv2` + `numpy` (`feature_detector.py:89`, `feature_matcher.py:119`, `pose_estimator.py:105`), and that without them every mode lands on `evidence-only` regardless of view count — which is what an 8-view run produced (`mode: standard`, `confidence: 0.49`).

Addressed in c343dbf. The runtime-capabilities documentation now states that the standard-library baseline always produces bounded evidence-only output, while metric pose/depth additionally requires calibration plus optional OpenCV and NumPy support. Those libraries are not project or CI dependencies.

Addressed in c343dbf. The protocol and public documentation now make this expected behavior explicit: without the optional metric solver, calibration cannot promote ordinary evidence into metric depth, so the result remains evidence-only rather than fabricating geometry.

Fixed in c343dbf. Filename classification now recognizes three-quarter, iso, oblique, and bare side labels. Three-quarter labels retain their visible direction tokens, while an unqualified side view remains side instead of becoming an arbitrary semantic pose.

Fixed in c343dbf. Classification now collects all delimited tokens and resolves the most specific observation instead of returning the first dictionary match. Added an eight-view regression case covering all four three-quarter directions, repeated front, rear, and side; it preserves seven semantic views rather than collapsing them into front.

Fixed in c343dbf. The classifier no longer creates false semantic duplicates from three-quarter labels. The output now also exposes semanticDuplicateViewCount and documents that it is semantic grouping only; strict image-duplicate detection remains owned by reference admission.

Fixed in c343dbf. The stage1b PNG readers now use the stage1 intake utility rather than stage4. The review adapter no longer imports Divine Eye; its caller injects the stage4 evaluator explicitly, so importing stage1b does not create a stage4 back-edge.

Fixed in c343dbf. Spec and build enhancers now retain multi-view provenance for an evidence-only brief but only apply component enhancement when components is a non-empty mapping. Added a regression test for the empty-components path.

Fixed in c343dbf. The checklist is now split into an evidence-only default gate and additional calibrated-envelope gates, so a successful evidence-only reconstruction is no longer asked to prove pose or depth.

Fixed in c343dbf. The protocol now has a Contradictory Views section: choose and record a metric authority, preserve conflicts as assumptions, and return request-input when the supplied views cannot be reconciled at the requested fidelity.

Addressed in c343dbf. The public documentation now has a Runtime capabilities section that separates coverage modes from metric capability and states the optional OpenCV and NumPy requirement for calibrated metric output.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Route unsupported CS2 families into adapter synthesis**

For the newly documented AWP/sniper and other non-knife CS2 paths, `forge/stage1_intake/cs2_manifest.py` still sets `state` to `unsupported-family`, omits `adapterStatus`, and exits with status 2; its validator also only permits `proceed` for knives. Consequently the mandatory CS2 manifest step hard-stops before the synthesized-adapter path described here can run. Update the manifest state machine to emit and accept the promised synthesis handoff.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce adapter validation in the gated build pipeline**

The adapter check is only advertised as a standalone command: the mandatory `strict-validation` checklist step still invokes only `validate_sculpt_spec.py`, that validator never calls this module, and `generate_threejs_factory.py` does not validate it either. Therefore the machine-enforced `forge/next.py` flow can mark validation complete and generate code from a spec with no adapter at all, bypassing the new before-code-generation requirement. Wire this validation into the existing strict validator or generator/checklist gate rather than relying on an untracked manual invocation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cross-check the adapter against the actual component tree**

When a spec contains a structurally valid adapter but an unrelated `componentTree`—for example, a mug adapter alongside a copied knife tree—`validate_spec()` returns success because it validates only the embedded adapter and never compares its component IDs or relationships with the geometry tree consumed by code generation. This permits exactly the generic fallback-tree mismatch the adaptive contract is intended to block; validate that adapter components and attachments correspond to the spec's actual component tree.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject attachment rules that reference unknown components**

For adapters containing attachment rules, `parent` and `child` are checked only for being non-empty strings, so a typo or wholly nonexistent component ID passes validation. The resulting contract no longer represents a valid parent-child/contact graph and cannot provide the promised attachment coverage. Check both endpoints against the collected component IDs and reject self-links or otherwise invalid graph edges.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Route calibration through the pre-spec synthesizer**

When `new_pre_spec_assessment.py` is invoked with the documented `--calibration` option, this parameter is never read and the function always returns the independent-evidence result without calling `synthesize_geometry_brief`. Consequently, even valid `cameraMatrix`, `focalLengthPx`, and `baselineUnits` data cannot produce the calibrated-depth envelope promised by the CLI and README, so the primary assessment-to-spec workflow silently discards its metric evidence.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep independent auto-clusters distinct**

For unnamed images whose signatures produce labels such as `auto-1` and `auto-2`, `_get_base_view_name` strips the trailing number from both labels, so this loop collapses every distinct cluster into the single key `auto`. A normal set of differently angled files such as `capture-a.png` and `capture-b.png` is therefore processed as one view, preventing feature matching and reporting an incorrect `viewCount`; only occurrence suffixes such as `auto-1-2` should be removed while preserving the cluster identifier.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve explicit scale without multi-view dimensions**

When a component has ordinary `dimensions` and an explicit `transform.scale`, this new ordering returns the dimensions first and ignores the authored transform. That reverses the previous precedence for all existing non-multi-view specs, so components whose transform intentionally differs from their descriptive dimensions are emitted at the wrong size; only `multiViewDimensions` should override the transform, while ordinary dimensions should remain the fallback.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retain every repeated --image in direct spec generation**

When users run `new_sculpt_spec.py` directly with repeated `--image` arguments and no assessment, only the first path is passed to `make_spec`, which consequently emits a one-element `sourceImages` array. This contradicts the repeatable CLI option and silently drops all rear/side references and their provenance; pass the complete list through or reject multiple images unless an assessment is supplied.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Let rejected views outrank low-confidence views**

When one compared view is a hard `reject` and another is `low-confidence`, this `any(...)` branch assigns the entire multi-view result `low-confidence` with action `probe`, masking the rejected view's required `refine-code` action. The aggregate should select `reject` whenever any view rejects, and only use `low-confidence` when no view has rejected.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Orient tapered-sweep sections perpendicular to the spine**

For the default tapered sweep, the spine runs along X, but every section offsets only X/Y while copying the spine point's Z unchanged. All vertices therefore lie in the same Z plane, so the advertised `thickness` does not create a volumetric blade and curved spines also receive sections in a fixed world plane rather than perpendicular to their tangent; construct a tangent/normal/binormal frame and apply the section offsets in that local frame.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve whitespace in installation target paths**

When `--target` contains whitespace, or when `$HOME` itself contains whitespace, this unquoted iteration splits the recorded directory into multiple targets. For example, `--target '/tmp/agent skills'` attempts to install first into `/tmp/agent/img2threejs` rather than the requested directory and may leave unintended files behind. Store targets without space-delimited encoding or iterate over them in a quoting-safe way.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use the configured showcase root for rig tests**

When the showcase checkout is not at this author's macOS path (for example CI or any contributor using `IMG2THREEJS_SHOWCASE_ROOT`), this hard-coded root makes both `setUpClass` methods raise before the env-configured showcase helper can run or skip. I confirmed `python3 -m unittest discover -s forge/tests -p 'test_*.py'` fails with `gate script not found at /Users/nhonh/Documents/personal/img2threejs-showcase/scripts/rig-milestone0.mjs`; use the existing `showcase_root()`/env path instead of pinning the separate companion repo to one machine.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L20-L21](https://github.com/img2threejs/img2threejs/blob/d0a72e1ea8ea7a062a4e5a5b060a9bd29f9bb30a/AGENTS.md#L20-L21)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make the alpha payload example pass its validator**

This documented example currently cannot be used: passing the JSON block above to `forge/stage5_rig/validate_rig_payload.py` returns `matrix_local[1] must have affine last row [0, 0, 0, 1]`, because the translation is placed in indices 12-14 while the validator accepts translation in the last column (indices 3/7/11). Users following the published alpha contract will get a failing payload, so either update the example/layout text or change the validator to match it.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L14-L14](https://github.com/img2threejs/img2threejs/blob/d0a72e1ea8ea7a062a4e5a5b060a9bd29f9bb30a/AGENTS.md#L14-L14)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the resumed pass when syncing a completed spec**

When a legitimately completed spec still contains the prior `continue` review, `current_pass()` returns `complete`; therefore the first `next.py` call after `state.py reset --force` passes `complete` here and immediately changes the rewound state back to `status=complete`. This makes the documented resume sequence unusable for the primary scenario this change targets, because the reset pass is discarded before any correction can be recorded.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Warn for normally completed states when work resumes**

For the stated fresh-session scenario, the old state is normally consistent: `status`, `currentPass`, and all final steps are complete. This predicate consequently returns false, so `next.py` prints no reset warning and continues to report the workflow as complete—the exact behavior the change is intended to prevent. The warning needs to cover a normal prior completion when invoked for resumed work, rather than only structurally inconsistent state files.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Re-run final checks after resetting a completed state**

When resetting a normally completed state, this clears only pass-scoped entries and leaves `part-coverage` and `action-ready` marked done with evidence from the pre-correction model. After the resumed pass changes the generated asset and transitions back to `complete`, `recompute()` accepts those stale final results and completes without revalidating coverage or interaction readiness.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep loop-ceiling states stopped during reset**

For a state stopped by `maxPerPass` or `maxTotal`, accepting `stopped` here sets it active without changing the retained loop counts or review history. The next mandatory `next.py` synchronization calculates the same ceiling and immediately hard-stops again, so the advertised stopped-state resume cannot actually continue; before that synchronization it also temporarily bypasses the hard-stop guard in `mark_steps()`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Grant pull request read permission**

When this workflow runs on a private/internal repo, the first GitHub API call in `list_pr_files()` is `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/files`, which GitHub documents as requiring `pull-requests: read` for private resources, and unspecified workflow permissions are set to `none` ([endpoint docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/pulls#fine-grained-access-tokens-for-list-pull-requests-files), [workflow permissions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#permissions)). With only `contents` and `issues` granted, the review step fails before it can build a context or post a comment; add `pull-requests: read` here.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Skip removed files before fetching head blobs**

When a PR deletes a text file, `list_pr_files()` still returns that filename with status `removed`, but this loop calls `get_pr_blob()` at the head SHA where the path no longer exists. The resulting GitHub contents 404 is raised before the `call_ai` try block, so the script exits as a setup failure without writing the review artifact or summary for deletion-only PRs; skip `removed` entries or treat that 404 as `None`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Update the nested pre-spec source image**

When this script regenerates the spec, it only overwrites the top-level `sourceImage`; the loaded starter's `preSpecAssessment.sourceImage` remains `/home/nyb/img2threejs/references/chinese-swords/汉代环首剑.jpg`, which is both a machine-local path and the wrong/nonexistent filename for this repo. Any assessment/review consumer that reads the nested pre-spec evidence will point at the stale reference even though the top-level field was corrected, so set the nested preSpecAssessment source from the same `SOURCE` before writing the spec and assessment.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include back-face decorations in ownership contract**

The Han subtype creates back-face `hamon-back-*`, `stud-back-*`, `stud-seat-back-*`, and `ring-engraving-back-*` components, but this ownership table closes after the front-side entries. Because `validate_dao_component_tree()` only checks IDs listed here, a missing or mis-owned back-side decoration still passes the family gate while the runtime contract expects both faces to move/select with the blade, handle, or ring modules; add the back-face IDs to the adapter.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**P1 — make this check conditional on using the plugin harness.** Lines 74–80 mandate `img2 doctor` and say it *must* pass before **every** reconstruction. However `docs/INSTALL.md` explicitly says the harness is optional for `generic`/base-only runs and that `img2 doctor` exits 1 when no harness is installed; `img2` may also have no launcher on PATH. A fresh user following Step 0 for a plain object is therefore blocked even though core `forge/` should run alone. Could we split this into a base-only preflight (`forge/state.py init --help`, etc.) and a required `img2 doctor/list` preflight **only when** a plugin profile is selected? A no-harness generic-run smoke test would preserve that contract.

**P2 — honor the `actionable` bit before publishing findings.** `normalize_review()` preserves `actionable: false` from the model, but `format_comment()` renders every entry in `findings` without checking it. Even an explicitly non-actionable/low-confidence model suggestion will appear under **Findings**, contrary to the prompt's 'only ... actionable and evidence-backed' contract. Drop non-actionable entries during normalization (or filter before rendering), and add a regression test where the model returns one `actionable: false` and one `actionable: true` finding so only the latter reaches the PR comment.

**P2 — this does not match `makeAttachmentEndpoint()` for partial attachments.** The generated TS calls `readVector3(record.localStart, [0,0,0])` and `readVector3(record.localEnd, [0,1,0])`, so an attachment object with one missing endpoint (e.g. a root `cylinder` with `attachment: {"localStart":[0,0,0]}`) still produces a non-null 1-unit endpoint. Here `_endpoint_would_be_null()` returns `True` instead, causing `validate_dimension_scale_consistency()` to warn that an identity scale overrides authored dimensions *even though the generator chooses endpoint-derived geometry rather than `scale_vector()`*. `validate_attachment()` currently allows missing endpoint fields when the attachment contract isn't required, so this is reachable. Please either mirror the TS endpoint defaults or reject incomplete endpoint declarations explicitly, with a regression for partial `attachment` objects.

**P2 — validator and emitted material disagree.** `check_material_physics('cloth', {'sheen': 0.7}, family='fabric')` reports missing `sheenColor` as a shader no-op, based on Three.js's black *library* default. But this pipeline's `generate_threejs_factory.py` emits `sheenColor: new THREE.Color(typeof spec.sheenColor === 'string' ? spec.sheenColor : '#ffffff')` (main line ~3353), so the **actual emitted** `MeshPhysicalMaterial` gets white and nonzero sheen. This means an existing valid render can be rejected for the wrong reason. Please align the validator with the emitted fallback (or deliberately change the generator with compatibility consideration), and add a spec-to-generated-material regression for the missing-color case. The doc's “both required” statement currently describes bare Three.js, not this generator.

**P2 — the standalone pass checker can accept an unvalidated textureless exemption.** `is_textureless()` only checks `textureless.declared is True`; the evidence/non-conflicting-channel requirements live in `validate_textureless()`. `orchestrate_passes.py check` calls `load_spec()` and `check_pass()` without `validate_spec()`, so a `textureless: {"declared":true}` entry with *no evidence* skips this quality bar and may report the material pass unlocked, while generator strict validation later blocks the same spec. Please validate the exemption here (or invoke the existing spec validator before `check`) so standalone pass-check results cannot contradict the hard gate; include a missing-evidence regression.

**P1 — Auggie's documented Node floor is too low.** This says `Node.js 20+`, but Augment's [official Auggie README](https://github.com/augmentcode/auggie#quick-start) explicitly says **Node 22+ required** for `npm install -g @augmentcode/auggie@latest`. A user on Node 20 is told they're supported and can end up with an unusable binary. Change this to `Node.js 22+`, make `node --version` a preflight, and add a Node 20 negative control to the doc/fixture QA. This extends @kokorolx's Pi runtime-prerequisite finding to the Auggie entry.

**P1 — the shown symlink is a directory, not a discoverable rule file.** This same document says Auggie reads `.augment/rules/*.md`, but the documented link `.augment/rules/img2threejs -> <your checkout>` resolves to a **directory** with no `.md` suffix. Deterministic negative control: `ln -s /tmp/skill .augment/rules/img2threejs && find .augment/rules -maxdepth 1 -name '*.md'` finds nothing; replacing it with `.augment/rules/img2threejs.md -> <your checkout>/SKILL.md` is picked up. The user-wide example has the same issue. Prefer a file symlink or the already documented `auggie --rules <path-to-SKILL.md>` and include a one-command existence/discovery check; this is static path validation, not a runtime Auggie execution claim.
